# CGRX v0.1.0-alpha.17

This prerelease adds exact declaration dependencies and reduces repeated TypeScript graph reconstruction work.

- Proves bounded named TypeScript imports and declaration-owned type, `typeof` and ordinary value references. Classes, interfaces, type aliases and plain variables remain distinct from callable identity. `find_usages` supports IMPORTS and REFERENCES scopes.
- Adds snapshot-bound definition selection for duplicate names and compacts symbol references while preserving exact identity, scope and freshness checks.
- Updates the bundled `cgrx-code-discovery` skill with exact `symbol_ref` selection, bounded import/reference queries, compact response decoding and freshness guidance.
- Improves native Python relative imports, Rust receiver/lifetime ownership and indexed Go field-receiver calls. Python lexical shadowing withdraws unsupported global call proofs and retains owned gaps.
- Binds SCIP confirmation to exact source-owned callee ranges and retires stale compiler proofs after source changes. Republishing an unchanged stale artifact cannot restore a withdrawn proof.
- Borrows current TypeScript facts and reuses augmentation and path-portability checks within one immutable graph reconstruction. On three paired process starts of the retained GD fixture, median opening time was 22.8s → 6.4s; VEX was 3.0s → 1.25s. These are local endpoint measurements with uncontrolled filesystem caches.
- Adds opt-in JavaScript identity/module evidence behind `experimental-javascript`. The published default build keeps JavaScript, PHP and Swift validation features disabled.

Unsupported module configuration, declaration merges, dynamic dispatch and callback targets remain explicit coverage gaps. Existing indexes with an older extraction or SCIP policy require reindexing; the old generation is preserved. The default extraction policy is 125 and SCIP policy is 3.

The Apple Silicon archive includes bundled web assets and `SHA256SUMS`. Linux and Intel macOS remain pinned source-install paths with Rust 1.89.0. This is an alpha release for testing.
